common_name: Bristol Fairy Baby's Breath (Double White Cut-Flower Perennial)

planting.note: Plant container-grown divisions in spring in deep, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Bristol Fairy resents transplanting once established due to its deep taproot, so choose the final site carefully.

directions: Plant container-grown divisions in deep, well-drained, slightly alkaline soil in full sun; Bristol Fairy is the classic fully double, pure-white-flowered baby's breath cultivar and the most widely grown of all Gypsophila selections, producing the same enormous airy clouds of tiny blooms as the species but with more substance and longer vase life thanks to its doubled petals. Like the species, it develops a deep taproot and resents disturbance once established, so plant from small containers while young rather than attempting to move a mature clump. Cutting stems for arrangements or deadheading spent flower sprays encourages continued bloom through midsummer. Best suited to zones 3-7; performs poorly and is often short-lived in hot, humid climates.

common_name: Lady Stratheden Geum (Semi-Double Golden Yellow Avens)

planting.note: Plant divisions or container plants in spring or early fall in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade; Lady Stratheden pairs classically with the scarlet-flowered 'Mrs. J. Bradshaw' for a two-tone geum display.

directions: Plant divisions or container plants in moist, humus-rich, well-drained soil in full sun to partial shade in zone 4-7; Lady Stratheden is one of the oldest and most widely grown geum cultivars, bearing warm golden-yellow, semi-double flowers held on branching stems above a mound of hairy, strawberry-like foliage from late spring into summer. It holds the Royal Horticultural Society's Award of Garden Merit and is traditionally planted alongside the scarlet 'Mrs. J. Bradshaw' as a classic cottage-garden combination. Deadhead spent flowers regularly to prolong bloom and encourage a repeat flush later in summer. Protect from hot afternoon sun in warm climates and divide congested clumps every 2-3 years in early fall.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Plants Database

planting.note: Plant grafted, container-grown or bare-root trees in moist, well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun to part shade; Vossii is propagated exclusively by grafting to preserve its exceptionally long flower chains and reduced seed set. ALL PARTS ARE HIGHLY TOXIC if ingested — keep away from children and pets.

directions: Plant grafted trees in moist, well-drained, slightly alkaline to neutral soil in full sun to part shade; Vossii is the finest and most widely planted selection of golden chain tree, producing exceptionally long, dense, pendulous racemes of clear-yellow pea flowers up to 20-24 inches long in May and June — considerably longer and more floriferous than the species — with the entire tree appearing to cascade in ropes of gold. It sets markedly fewer seed pods than the straight species, somewhat reducing (though not eliminating) the toxicity hazard. Vossii is the cultivar most often trained over an arched tunnel or pergola, as in the famous Laburnum Walk at Bodnant Garden in Wales. Tolerant of shallow, chalky soils and part shade. EXTREME CAUTION: all parts of the plant, especially the seed pods and seeds, contain cytisine, a toxic alkaloid, and are highly poisonous — never plant where children play.

common_name: Pacific Sunset Maple (Shantung x Norway Hybrid Street Tree)

planting.note: Plant grafted, container-grown trees in moist, well-drained soil in spring or fall; Pacific Sunset is a patented hybrid propagated only by grafting and is widely used as a compact, uniform street and parking-lot tree.

directions: Plant grafted trees in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to part shade; Pacific Sunset is a hybrid between Shantung maple and Norway maple selected for a dense, uniform, rounded-oval canopy and reliable orange-red fall color, combining the heat, drought, and alkaline-soil tolerance of A. truncatum with the vigor and symmetry prized in a street tree. It grows 25-35 feet tall with a tidy, low-maintenance form that has made it a popular choice for parking lots, medians, and residential street plantings across the western and central United States. New spring growth emerges with a purple-red tinge before turning glossy green through summer. Like its sibling selection 'Norwegian Sunset', it is non-invasive and far better behaved than straight Norway maple, without the aggressive seeding and surface rooting that plague that species.

common_name: Norwegian Sunset Maple (Shantung x Norway Hybrid Street Tree)

planting.note: Plant grafted, container-grown trees in moist, well-drained soil in spring or fall; Norwegian Sunset is a patented hybrid propagated only by grafting and is planted extensively as a uniform, upright street and parking-lot tree.

directions: Plant grafted trees in well-drained, moderately fertile soil in full sun to part shade; Norwegian Sunset is a hybrid between Shantung maple and Norway maple selected for a more upright, symmetrical, oval-to-pyramidal canopy than its rounder sibling selection 'Pacific Sunset', combining the heat and drought tolerance of A. truncatum with vigorous, uniform growth. It reaches 30-35 feet with a tidy branching habit and develops dependable orange to red-orange fall color, making it a favorite of municipal street tree and parking lot programs across the western and central United States. New spring foliage emerges with a reddish-purple cast before turning deep green through the growing season. Non-invasive and far better behaved than straight Norway maple, without the aggressive self-seeding of that species.

common_name: Malayan Dwarf Coconut Palm (Compact Early-Bearing Selection)

planting.note: Plant container-grown seedlings or place a partly husked seed nut on its side with one-third buried in moist, well-drained, sandy to loamy soil in full sun after all frost danger has passed; Malayan Dwarf comes true from seed because it is naturally self-pollinating, unlike many taller coconut varieties.

directions: Plant container-grown seedlings or a partly husked seed nut in well-drained, sandy to loamy soil in full sun; Malayan Dwarf is the most widely planted dwarf coconut selection, valued for its compact 20-30 foot mature height (roughly half that of tall varieties), earlier bearing at just 4-6 years from planting, and moderate resistance to lethal yellowing disease that has devastated tall coconut plantings throughout Florida and the Caribbean. Because it is naturally self-pollinating, seed nuts come true to type, making it easy to propagate reliably from seed. The shorter stature also makes harvesting and hurricane cleanup considerably safer and easier than with tall varieties. Golden, green, or yellow-fruited strains are all sold under the Malayan Dwarf name. Extremely frost-sensitive — restricted to USDA zones 10-12 in the continental US, chiefly southern Florida and Hawaii.
sources: University of Hawaii at Manoa Cooperative Extension

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown specimens in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade in spring; Lalandei is one of the oldest and most cold-hardy firethorn selections, dating to the 1870s.

directions: Root semi-hardwood cuttings or plant container specimens in well-drained, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to partial shade; Lalandei is one of the oldest and most vigorous firethorn cultivars still widely grown, dating from the 1870s, and is valued for its reliably heavy fall crop of large orange-red berries, upright vase-shaped habit, and slightly better cold hardiness than many newer selections. It grows larger and more rangy than compact modern cultivars, making it well suited to a big informal barrier hedge, espalier against a wall, or a freestanding specimen given room to spread. White flower clusters in spring draw pollinators before the berries color up in autumn, and cedar waxwings, robins, and mockingbirds flock to the fruit through winter. The vigorous, thorny growth benefits from pruning right after spring bloom if size control is needed. Berries are mildly toxic to humans; do not eat.
sources: North Carolina State Extension — Plants Database
Clemson Cooperative Extension Home & Garden Information Center

planting.note: Divide established clumps in spring or plant container-grown plants in almost any well-drained to moist soil in full sun to full shade; Tanika is propagated exclusively by division or tissue culture rather than seed, and is the most widely sold Lomandra selection in commercial landscaping.

directions: Plant in virtually any well-drained soil in full sun to full shade; Tanika is a compact selection of mat rush bred for finer, softer, more graceful strap-like foliage and a neater, more uniform mounded habit than the species, making it the dominant Lomandra cultivar used in commercial and municipal landscaping worldwide. Like the species it is extraordinarily tolerant of drought, heat, poor soil, salt spray, periodic waterlogging, and shade, and needs essentially no supplemental water once established in zone 8+. Small, cream-yellow, sweetly fragrant flower clusters appear in late spring just above or within the fine foliage. Its smaller, tidier size compared to the straight species suits it to mass planting along walkways, streetscapes, and highway medians, as a no-maintenance edging plant, or in dry shade under trees where few other grass-like plants thrive.

common_name: Sulphur Heart Persian Ivy (Yellow-Centered Variegated Vine)

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring or fall in any well-drained soil in shade; Sulphur Heart (also sold as 'Paddy's Pride') holds its bold yellow leaf centers best with some direct morning or filtered sun.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in partial shade to full shade — light filtered sun helps intensify the variegation; Sulphur Heart (also widely sold as 'Paddy's Pride') is the classic bold, large-leaved variegated Persian ivy, with glossy, heart-shaped leaves 6-8 inches across that are broadly splashed with bright sulfur-yellow at the center and irregularly margined in dark green, creating a strikingly bright accent in shaded areas where most variegated plants struggle. Like the species, it climbs by aerial rootlets and tolerates deep shade far better than English ivy, while remaining much less prone to escaping into natural areas in North America. Excellent trained on a shaded wall or trellis, as a groundcover under trees, or cascading from a large container. Berries are toxic — do not plant where children or pets may ingest them.

planting.note: Plant rooted cuttings or container stock in spring or fall in any well-drained soil in shade; Dentata Variegata establishes quickly and, like other Persian ivy cultivars, is less prone to leaf spot and spider mite problems than English ivy in hot, humid summers.

directions: Plant in well-drained soil in partial shade to full shade; Dentata Variegata is a large-leaved variegated Persian ivy cultivar with broad, heart-shaped, slightly toothed leaves showing gray-green marbled centers and irregular creamy-white to pale yellow margins, giving a softer, more subtly variegated effect than the bolder yellow-centered 'Sulphur Heart'. Like the species, it climbs readily by aerial rootlets, tolerates deep shade far better than English ivy, and is considerably less likely to escape cultivation than that more aggressive relative. The oversized leaves, up to 8 inches across, give it a bold, almost tropical texture well suited to shaded walls, fences, and trellises, or as a groundcover under trees. Berries are toxic — do not plant where children or pets may ingest them.

common_name: Wynyabbie Gem Australian Rosemary (Lavender-Mauve Flowering Hybrid)

planting.note: Root semi-hardwood cuttings in summer or plant container-grown plants in well-drained, lean, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to part shade; Wynyabbie Gem is a naturally occurring hybrid between W. fruticosa and W. eremicola valued for its more consistent lavender-mauve flowering.

directions: Plant in well-drained, lean, slightly acidic to neutral soil in full sun to part shade; Wynyabbie Gem is a vigorous natural hybrid between coastal rosemary (Westringia fruticosa) and the inland species W. eremicola, combining a denser, more upright habit with more consistently produced lavender-mauve flowers than the straight species, which typically blooms white to very pale lavender. It grows into a substantial rounded shrub, useful as an informal hedge, screen, or freestanding specimen in hot, dry, coastal or inland landscapes, and like its parent species tolerates salt spray, poor soil, and extended drought once established. Flowers appear nearly year-round in mild climates, providing a steady nectar source for bees. Lightly shear after flowering flushes to maintain a dense, compact form.
